stemLabel: OZ — winger has it on the wall, weak-side D stepping toward the net

read.cue: the weak-side defenceman is beginning to step toward the net — they haven't arrived yet, but they're on their way

interaction.prompt: Your winger has the puck on the wall and the weak-side defenceman is beginning to step toward the net. Drag YOURSELF to the best spot to receive.

feedback.right: Good read. You saw the D stepping toward the net and got to the weak-side wall before they could lock it down — now your winger has the cross-ice look.
feedback.wrong: Watch the D's feet. They're moving toward the net, which means they're about to cover net-front. The ice they're vacating — the weak-side wall — is where you want to be.

tip: Attack the space the defence leaves. When a defender drops to the net, the ice they vacated is the open one.
why: Reading the off-puck defender is the difference between skating into coverage and finding open ice. The D's choice tells you where to go.
